front: What does `touch NAME` do?
back: It creates an empty file if the name doesn’t exist. If it does exist, `touch` only updates its modification time and leaves the content alone.

front: What does `mkdir -p levels/world1/boss` do that plain `mkdir` doesn’t?
back: `-p` (parents) creates the whole chain of directories and doesn’t complain if one already exists. Plain `mkdir` fails when the parent is missing.

front: When does `rmdir` work?
back: Only on an empty directory, which makes it the safe way to clean up. For a directory with content you need `rm -r`.

front: What does `cp hero1.png backup` do when `backup` is an existing directory?
back: It puts the copy inside the directory under the same name. If `backup` didn’t exist, it would be the name of a new file.

front: Mira types `cp backup backup2` for a directory and gets an error. What is missing?
back: `-r` (recursive): `cp -r backup backup2`. Without it `cp` omits directories.

front: What do `cp -i` and `cp -v` do?
back: `-i` asks before overwriting an existing file. `-v` prints what is being done. Without `-i`, `cp` silently replaces an existing destination.

front: How do you rename a file in Linux?
back: With `mv`, for example `mv slime.png blob.png`. There is no separate rename command: `mv` moves it, or renames it when the destination is a new name in the same place.

front: Does `mv` need `-r` for directories?
back: No. It moves directories without options. Like `cp`, it overwrites an existing destination without asking unless you use `-i`.

front: What are `rm -r`, `rm -i` and `rm -f`?
back: `-r` deletes directories and everything in them, `-i` asks before every removal and `-f` forces: it never asks and ignores missing files.

front: Is there a trash can for `rm`?
back: No. On the command line a deleted file is gone for good, and `rm -rf` removes a whole tree silently.

front: How can Mira see what `rm *.png` would delete before running it?
back: Put `echo` in front: `echo rm *.png` shows what the shell would pass and deletes nothing.

front: What does `rm somedir` print for a directory, and how do you remove it?
back: `rm: cannot remove 'somedir': Is a directory`. Use `rm -r somedir` (or `rmdir` if it is empty).

front: Which commands create, copy, move, delete files and make or remove directories?
back: `touch` creates a file, `cp` copies, `mv` moves or renames, `rm` deletes, `mkdir` makes a directory and `rmdir` removes an empty one.

front: Are `notes.txt`, `Notes.txt` and `NOTES.TXT` the same file on Linux?
back: No. File names are case sensitive, so these are three different names that can live side by side. The same goes for commands and options (`-r` and `-R` can differ).

front: `cat NOTES.TXT` says "No such file or directory", but `notes.txt` exists. Why?
back: A name that is right except for the case doesn’t exist on Linux. Use the exact case.

front: What happens if Mira runs `mv notes.txt Notes.txt` while both exist?
back: `notes.txt` overwrites `Notes.txt` without asking, since they are different files. `mv -i` would ask first.

front: What do `*` and `?` match in a glob?
back: `*` matches any number of any characters, including none. `?` matches exactly one character.

front: What do `[abc]`, `[a-z]` and `[!abc]` match?
back: One character from the list, one character in the range, and one character that is not in the list.

front: Which of `boss1.png`, `boss2.png` and `boss10.png` does `boss?.png` match?
back: `boss1.png` and `boss2.png`, not `boss10.png`: the `?` is exactly one character.

front: Which files does `hero[12].png` match among `hero1.png`, `hero2.png` and `hero3.png`?
back: `hero1.png` and `hero2.png`, not `hero3.png`.

front: Who expands a glob, the shell or the command?
back: The shell, before the command runs, into all matching names sorted. The command never sees the pattern.

front: What happens with `ls *.jpg` when no file matches?
back: Bash passes the pattern unchanged, so `ls` complains: `cannot access '*.jpg': No such file or directory`.

front: Do `*` and `?` match hidden files?
back: No. They don’t match a leading dot, so hidden files stay out unless the dot is written explicitly.

front: How do you stop the shell from expanding `*`?
back: Quote it: `echo "*"` prints a star, which is how a pattern reaches a command that expands it itself.

front: Which glob notations match one character that is not in a set, or one digit?
back: `[!abc]` and `[^abc]` match one character not listed. `[[:digit:]]` matches one digit; other classes are `[:alpha:]`, `[:upper:]`, `[:lower:]` and `[:alnum:]`.

front: What happens to the copy when you run `cp -r dir dest`?
back: If `dest` exists, the copy lands inside it as `dest/dir`. If it doesn't, the copy is named `dest`.

front: What does `echo text > file` do if `file` already exists?
back: It silently replaces the content. `>>` appends instead.
